description: Registry of clause tags for docs that carry stable clause identifiers and normative language. Tags: 'check-exists' — a named, runnable check already guards the clause (check-ref points at it); 'checkable' — a mechanical check can guard the clause but is not built yet (check-ref names the intended check and any interim probe); 'judgment-only' — compliance is a per-change judgment no check can decide (justification says why). Clause identifiers are stable: never renumbered, and a retired identifier stays reserved (listed under 'retired'). A row that states a check-ref may also carry 'test-cases': the identifiers of the test cases pinning the clause, each of which the registry check resolves as a literal in one of the files that row's check-ref cites by path — a suite file, or a source file whose in-crate test module states the case. The field is opt-in, and stating it is what puts those identifiers under the check.

scripts/check-schema-echo.js walks every object subschema of every composed platform's schema — composed in-process from the source layers, never the published copies under schemas/dist/, which lag between releases — and holds each to the posture its class states: action objects declare no additionalProperties, the user-defined metadata maps declare a typed-value additionalProperties schema, the discriminating oneOf hosts declare none, and every other object declares additionalProperties: false. No exemption is taken by name alone: a def registered as a discriminating host must still state oneOf members, the action wrapper's members and the defs carrying the action prefix are diffed both ways, and each metadata host must reference the one map definition rather than restate it (an inline copy is refused, so the walk judges one definition and not each copy) with that definition's value schema stating what a value may be. A def outside every registered class is judged as a closed object, so it reds unless it declares additionalProperties: false (npm run lint:schema-echo, a step in CI's lint job). Residue: the walk judges an object subschema when it states type object or carries properties and sits under one of the composition keywords the walk descends — a schema written outside that reach goes unjudged rather than red; and the check holds its posture model against the schemas in that direction only — it never reads this clause's sentence, so a change to either side leaves their agreement a review judgment; the prose gloss (that fields may be added in minor versions and consumers should ignore unknown ones), and whether a newly opened object is genuinely an evolution surface, stay review-held too.

The recorder's registrations sit outside the mirrored capture block, so the one production copy is what is read; the block itself stays held by the parity test. Named residue: a registration shape outside the scan's model is refused rather than skipped — an event name that is not a lone string literal (a concatenated name is refused, never read as its leading fragment), a receiver outside document and window, which is what a helper taking its target as a parameter looks like wherever that helper is defined, and an addListener chain not rooted at chrome. What is genuinely invisible is a registration site that lands in neither scanned file: a helper defined elsewhere and merely called here registers nothing these two files show. Beyond that, the capture phase this clause also states is not read — the scan parses no listener options, so the phase claim stays review-held — and whether a handler still captures what its enumeration entry describes is review-held.

scripts/check-extension-surface.js (npm run lint:extension-surface, a step in CI's lint job) reads the worker dispatcher (packages/extension/background/service-worker.js) through the shared comment-safe tokenizer: the one switch over the message type — brace-depth bounded, required to carry a default: arm (presence-checked; the envelope it answers is ERT-2's own verification) — has its case labels diffed both ways against the panel protocol's Types cells, and the module's message-type equality literals are diffed both ways against the capture-path table's types. The sender side is read the same way, over the tracked JavaScript under packages/extension/sidepanel/ (git ls-files over that directory, recursive, filtered by extension): a send call whose first argument opens an object literal is read, that literal's top-level properties (brace-depth bounded, so a nested payload's own type is never read as the message's) scanned for a type key — bare or quoted, in any position, since property order carries no meaning — carrying a lone string literal, with the token after that literal required to be the property separator or the literal's closing brace, so a concatenation is refused instead of being credited with its leading piece; a send stating no such property is refused by name, and the diagnosis names what the scan found in its place rather than the key it wanted. The types those calls state are diffed both ways against the same panel-protocol enumeration, and the clause's own sender statement (the runtime doc's panel-sends-literally paragraph inside ERT-4) is the doctrine that leg holds. The two doc enumerations must be disjoint, every cell must be a lone backticked name, and empty parses and anchor failures (a missing or second dispatcher switch, a missing default: arm, a nested dispatcher) fail loudly. Named residue: the equality scan is module-wide and deduplicated, not listener-scoped — the clause's ahead-of-the-switch mechanism and the guards' placement are review-held (token order is not control flow); a dispatch route outside the tokenized shapes (a computed message type, a negated or reversed-operand type test, an equality test on another receiver) is invisible to the scan; a regular-expression literal carrying a brace inside the dispatcher body corrupts the depth bound and reds with a misleading diagnosis (loud, never green), and the same unmodelled class costs the whole-file send scan silently — a quote inside a regular-expression literal desynchronizes the token stream for the rest of that file, and the send sites past it are simply not seen. The panel table's sender-side claim is held over the literal-send subset the scan reads, and carries residues of its own, each named here: a send-shaped site whose first argument is anything but an opening object literal sits outside that subset and is invisible here — the function and method-shorthand declarations (packages/extension/sidepanel/panel.js, packages/extension/sidepanel/adapter-chrome.js), the receiver-qualified forward, and the call passing a payload assembled beforehand are all that shape — and, in the reverse direction, an enumerated type sent only through such a site reds as never sent, a misleading red this direction cannot tell from a genuinely unsent type. The tables' rationale, payload, and response prose stays review-held.

Flag detection is token-exact, so the --lint both gates already pass never reads as --lint-strict. The watch is also held to the tree it watches, so a correct verdict cannot be computed over the wrong files: each gate command's own --platform and --baseline argument values must equal the platform and baseline the check reads for it (as must the --baseline of npm run sufficiency:check, the file the fail-class population comes from), and the platforms corpus/manifest.json carries sessions for are diffed against the watched set both ways — a platform the corpus grows that the watch has not learned reds rather than going unwatched, and a watched platform the catalogue no longer carries reds equally. Every input is guarded before it is believed: a baseline with no keys, or one missing a key for an active session, is a machinery verdict naming the file rather than an emptiness that would demand the flip. Residue: whether a flipped gate then stays green is the comparator's own business, not this watch's, and the whole-file npm run sufficiency:check surface is deliberately unwatched for the grounds the check's header records.
